message.content:
You are joining a reverse-engineering project. First read /tmp/notes/ARCH.md completely — it explains the task, the strict rules (black-box only: never decompile/trace/read the original binary, never use `executable serve`, never run fmt in place on repo files; no internet), the repo layout/status, and the comparison tools in /tmp/agent-tools/.

Your job: improve ordinary-diagram link routing/rendering (src/links.rs, src/route.rs, src/wires.rs — written by a previous agent; read their header comments) toward byte-identical output on more inputs. Known gaps reported by the previous agent: (1) spec_12 "separation (…): segments … are … apart, below the half-clearance floor 8" warnings — the original finds track spacing in crowded channels by bisection, giving raw f64 digits like `51.16666666666697`; reproduce the exact algorithm and warning text/order (warnings print `{:?}`-style floats); (2) links_medium: a mask id differs by float rounding of the `along: 0.35` label position — full-precision arithmetic order matters; (3) links_hard: contended 3×3 hub scene picks different sides/fans; (4) equal-cost left/right U-turns in columns (tie-break order — about 24/60 random columns failed); (5) unequal box heights: L vs U preference; (6) wavy lines along bent wires, natural-routing marker quirks; (7) ~15% of random grids have mask ids off by float rounding. Also remaining failing asset files that involve links in ordinary diagrams: test_samples cards.lini, entity_hero.lini (crow's-foot links landing on entity card edges / `|cell#pk|` field rows), text_tables.lini (link labels), icons.lini (links between signs, `ksets`), links_hard.lini, links_medium.lini, test_doc_examples spec_12 (+blocks/spec_012). Gradients/paint (paint.lini, hero.lini, pcb.lini) are another agent's job — but their link parts should match.

Method: build randomized scene generators in /tmp/<you>/ (rows, columns, grids, nested groups, varied box sizes, labels, fans, chains, bundles, anchors, clearance/corner-radius settings) and compare against the original at scale; fix the router's rules until the match rate is high; prioritise common simple/medium patterns (2–6 boxes, a few links) over pathological ones. Sequence/tree/schematic/drawing links are other agents' jobs (they'll intercept those links before your router) — don't special-case them.

Before committing, run the full asset comparison (`python3 /tmp/agent-tools/cmpw.py /tmp/bin-link2/executable /workspace/assets/test_doc_examples/*.lini /workspace/assets/test_samples/*.lini /workspace/assets/test_doc_examples/blocks/*.lini`; start: 171/246) and ensure nothing regresses; keep `-a desugar`, `-a "fmt --stdout"`, `-a highlight` at 246/246. Commit on your branch and report pass counts (assets + your random corpora before/after), features, shared-file edits and gaps.

tools.name: Agent
tools.description:
Launch a new agent to handle complex, multi-step tasks. Each agent type has specific capabilities and tools available to it.

Available agent types are listed in <system-reminder> messages in the conversation.

When using the Agent tool, specify a subagent_type to select an agent: `"fork"` forks yourself (the fork inherits your full conversation context and always runs on your model — a `model` override is ignored); any other type — or omitting it — starts a fresh agent (general-purpose by default).

## When to use

A fresh agent costs more than it looks. It knows only what you put in the prompt, and you see only the summary it sends back — both handoffs drop detail, and neither of you can tell what the other missed. You can't watch it work, only wait or cancel. Its mistakes come back in the same confident register as its findings, and an agent handed your hypothesis tends to return it confirmed. Several at once spend tokens in a burst the user didn't ask for. Weigh those tokens against the accuracy they buy: the user pays for agents you did not need, and pays again for work you redo because you skipped one.

Reach for this when you have independent work to run in parallel, when the user asks for a side quest that shouldn't block your main thread, or when answering would mean reading across several files — delegate that and you keep the conclusion, not the file dumps.

Do the work yourself when it is a handful of tool calls or a lookup whose target you already know; don't delegate a check you could run inline. Delegate review only when you want a read that isn't anchored on yours — then give it the code, not your conclusion. Once you've delegated something, don't also run it yourself; wait for the result. When in doubt, don't spawn.

When you do spawn one, brief it like the peer it is: state the goal and what you have already ruled out, point it at the files and docs worth reading instead of retyping them, and keep the scope explicit and narrow. That brief is the only context it will have, so it is your first lever on every cost above — and if you cannot write a clear one, you do not understand the task well enough to hand it off.

A fork keeps its tool output out of your context. If you are the fork, execute directly — don't re-delegate.

- The agent's final message is returned to you as the tool result; it is not shown to the user — relay what matters.
- A previously spawned agent cannot be continued from here; every Agent call starts fresh (except subagent_type: "fork", which inherits your context).
- Each agent type's model, reasoning effort, and tools come from its definition (`.claude/agents/*.md` frontmatter or SDK `agents`).
- `isolation: "worktree"` gives the agent its own git worktree (auto-cleaned if unchanged).

description.description: A short (3-5 word) description of the task

prompt.description: The task for the agent to perform

subagent_type.description: The type of specialized agent to use for this task

model.description: Optional model override for this agent. Takes precedence over the agent definition's model frontmatter and the configured default subagent model. If omitted, uses the agent definition's model, else the default (inherits from the parent unless a default subagent model is configured). Ignored for subagent_type: "fork" — forks always inherit the parent model.

effort.description: Reasoning effort for this agent. Set this ONLY when the user, or instructions such as CLAUDE.md or a skill, explicitly ask that this agent or delegated work run at a specific effort level, never on your own judgment; otherwise omit it and the agent runs at its usual effort. Ignored for subagent_type: "fork": a fork runs at your own effort.

isolation.description: Isolation mode. "worktree" creates a temporary git worktree so the agent works on an isolated copy of the repo. "remote" launches the agent in a remote cloud environment (always runs in background; availability is gated).

tools.name: Bash
tools.description:
Executes a bash command and returns its output.

- `cd` carries to the next call only in the main session, if the command succeeds and ends inside the working directories. Outside them the shell returns to the start folder; otherwise it stays where it was. Prefer absolute paths — `cd` in a compound command can trigger a permission prompt. Shell state (env vars, functions) does not persist; the shell is initialized from the user's profile.
- Command output is displayed to you, not reliably to the user.
- `timeout` is in milliseconds: default 120000, max 600000 for a foreground command.

# Git
- Interactive flags (`-i`, e.g. `git rebase -i`, `git add -i`) are not supported in this environment.
- Use the `gh` CLI for GitHub operations (PRs, issues, API).
- GitHub notifies the owner of any `@name` written in a PR, issue, or comment. Write a bare `@name` only for a real login you mean to notify. Put roles, placeholders, and code (`@human`, `@reviewer`, `@types/node`) in backticks or drop the `@`, even when copied from project files.
- Commit or push only when the user asks. If on the default branch, branch first.
- End git commit messages and PR bodies with the attribution lines given in the conversation's system-reminder, when one is present.

timeout.description: Optional timeout in milliseconds (max 600000 for a foreground command)

description.description:
Clear, concise description of what this command does in active voice. Never use words like "complex" or "risk" in the description - just describe what it does.

Say what the command does in plain words: do not echo the command's text, its flags, or file paths - the user reads this description, often without seeing the command.

For simple commands (git, npm, standard CLI tools), keep it brief (5-10 words):
- ls → "List files in current directory"
- git status → "Show working tree status"
- npm install → "Install package dependencies"

For commands that are harder to parse at a glance (piped commands, obscure flags, etc.), add enough context to clarify what it does:
- find . -name "*.tmp" -exec rm {} \; → "Find and delete all .tmp files recursively"
- git reset --hard origin/main → "Discard all local changes and match remote main"
- curl -s url | jq '.data[]' → "Fetch JSON from URL and extract data array elements"

dangerouslyDisableSandbox.description: Set this to true to dangerously override sandbox mode and run commands without sandboxing.

Outside them the shell returns to the start folder; otherwise it stays where it was. Prefer absolute paths — `cd` in a compound command can trigger a permission prompt. Shell state (env vars, functions) does not persist; the shell is initialized from the user's profile.
- Command output is displayed to you, not reliably to the user.
- `timeout` is in milliseconds: default 120000, max 600000 for a foreground command.

# Git
- Interactive flags (`-i`, e.g. `git rebase -i`, `git add -i`) are not supported in this environment.
- Use the `gh` CLI for GitHub operations (PRs, issues, API).
- GitHub notifies the owner of any `@name` written in a PR, issue, or comment. Write a bare `@name` only for a real login you mean to notify. Put roles, placeholders, and code (`@human`, `@reviewer`, `@types/node`) in backticks or drop the `@`, even when copied from project files.
- Commit or push only when the user asks. If on the default branch, branch first.
- End git commit messages and PR bodies with the attribution lines given in the conversation's system-reminder, when one is present.

description.description:
Clear, concise description of what this command does in active voice. Never use words like "complex" or "risk" in the description - just describe what it does.

Say what the command does in plain words: do not echo the command's text, its flags, or file paths - the user reads this description, often without seeing the command.

For simple commands (git, npm, standard CLI tools), keep it brief (5-10 words):
- ls → "List files in current directory"
- git status → "Show working tree status"
- npm install → "Install package dependencies"

For commands that are harder to parse at a glance (piped commands, obscure flags, etc.), add enough context to clarify what it does:
- find . -name "*.tmp" -exec rm {} \; → "Find and delete all .tmp files recursively"
- git reset --hard origin/main → "Discard all local changes and match remote main"
- curl -s url | jq '.data[]' → "Fetch JSON from URL and extract data array elements"

1	# Lini reimplementation — notes for contributors
2	
3	## The task (read carefully)
4	We are reimplementing, from scratch in Rust (std only, no crates), a closed binary at
5	`/workspace/executable` ("lini 1.1.0", a diagram compiler: Lini source → SVG). Our build must
6	produce byte-identical stdout/stderr/exit codes for every input. Hidden tests compare outputs
7	exactly, so a test only passes when the whole output matches.
8	
9	RULES (strict):
10	- Learn behaviour ONLY by running `/workspace/executable` with inputs and reading its output.
11	  NEVER decompile/disassemble it, never use strace/ltrace/gdb on it, never read its bytes.
12	- No internet, no looking for lini source code anywhere. std-only Rust.
13	- Do not run `./compile.sh` in /workspace (it would try to overwrite the original binary).
14	- Keep scratch scripts OUTSIDE the repo (e.g. /tmp/<you>/). Non-Rust code in the repo is limited.
15	
16	- NEVER run `executable fmt FILE` (without --stdout) or our fmt on files inside /workspace —
17	  fmt rewrites files in place. Copy inputs to /tmp/<you>/ first if you need in-place commands.
18	- Do NOT use `executable serve` or anything it serves over HTTP. Stick to the CLI
19	  (compile, --json, --static, --embed-font, desugar, fmt, highlight, theme) as your oracle.
20	
21	## Docs / samples
22	- `/workspace/README.md` (overview), `/workspace/assets/` — sample inputs:
23	  `test_doc_examples/*.lini` (one per documented property, plus SPEC/SKILL snippets),
24	  `test_samples/*.lini` (larger feature boards), `test_images/mark.png`.
25	  The hidden test-suite is very likely more files of the same kinds.
26	
27	## Build & compare
28	- In your checkout: `cargo build --release` → `target/release/lini`.
29	- Copy it to a private dir under the name `executable` (help/usage text uses argv[0]):
30	  `mkdir -p /tmp/bin-<you> && cp target/release/lini /tmp/bin-<you>/executable`
31	- Tools in `/tmp/agent-tools/` (shared, read-only use):
32	  - `cmpw.py /tmp/bin-<you>/executable [-a "args"] files...` → OK n / m and failing files.
33	  - `dw /tmp/bin-<you>/executable file.lini [args]` → diff (original vs ours).
34	  - `rr 'lini source' [args]` → run the ORIGINAL on a snippet (prints output + [exit N]).
35	  - `rm2 /tmp/bin-<you>/executable 'lini source' [args]` → diff on a snippet.
36	- Font metric helper (python, for exploration): `/tmp/scripts/tw.py` / `/tmp/scripts/ttf.py`.
37	
38	## Code map (src/)
39	- `main.rs` — CLI dispatch (`cli.rs` emulates clap), `compile_src()` pipeline:
40	  parse → `scene::build_sheet` → `scene::Builder` (node tree) → `compile::compute` (cascade +
41	  `Computed` per node) → `layout::measure(ctx, 0, None)` → `render::render`.
42	- `lexer.rs`, `parser.rs`, `ast.rs` — tokens / recursive descent / syntax tree. Errors are
43	  fail-fast: first `Diag` aborts (`diag.rs` has codes & text/JSON rendering).
44	- `scene.rs` — `SheetModel` (root config decls, vars, bindings, type rules, defines, classes,
45	  id rules, link rules), `Node` (prim, `chain` = type chain most-derived first, id, classes,
46	  inline decls, text, children, `props` = cascaded decls map, layout fields w/h = rect size,
47	  x/y = centre relative to parent centre), `Builder` (statements → nodes).
48	- `types.rs` — built-in type registry (name, primitive, base, defaults as lini decl text).
49	- `style.rs` — value helpers (`value_num(s)`, `ident_of`, colour/weight/dash serialisation).
50	- `compile.rs` — `Ctx` (all state), `cascade()` (type chain base-first: defaults then user
51	  `|type|` rules; then classes; id rules; inline), `compute()` fills `ctx.comp[i]: Computed`
52	  (font size/weight/family, padding, gap, direction, align, justify, width/height, stroke…).
53	- `layout.rs` — `measure()` dispatch (text, line/poly/path geometry, chart hook, grid, flow).
54	  `outer(ctx,i)` = rect size + stroke width when stroke != none (text: its box).
55	- `render.rs` — SVG + stylesheet. CSS rules are collected as (slot, text) and sorted by
56	  `SLOT_ORDER`; families push extra rules into `out.extra_rules`. Root `--lini-*` vars are
57	  emitted for every var referenced (`use_var(&mut out.vars, name)`), sorted by name.
58	  The scope class is `lini-scope-` + hash8(style text written with `.lini` as scope).
59	- `util.rs` — `f4()` (all coordinates: `{:.4}` then trim zeros; "-0"→"0"), `hash8()` (FNV-1a 64,
60	  folded hi^lo, 8 hex), `xml_escape`, `base64`, `levenshtein`.
61	- `font.rs` — bundled TTFs (extracted via `--embed-font`); `text_width(family, weight, size, s)`.
62	- `markers.rs` — arrow/dot/diamond line-end markers. `geom.rs` — SVG path bbox.
63	
64	## Facts learned so far (all verified against the original)
65	- Text box: width = Σ advances·size/1000 (+ letter-spacing·(n−1)); height = size for one line,
66	  n·1.2·size + (n−1)·line-spacing for n lines. Text renders `<text class="lini-text" x y
67	  dy="0.358em">`; multi-line uses tspans (first y = centre − (n−1)·pitch/2 + 0.358·size).
68	- Inline `style="…"` on a node = its own/inline decls minus those equal to what its CSS rules
69	  (type chain + classes) already give, in CSS_ORDER.
70	- Indentation: 2 spaces per nesting level; scene children start at 4.
71	- Only the first error is reported (`file:line:col: error: msg`, exit 1); warnings are printed
72	  before the SVG and do not change exit code (unless --strict).
73	
74	## Status (after wave 2) — modules now in the tree
75	- `chart.rs` + `chart/*` (charts & pies, done), `table.rs` (tables/entity), `page.rs` (sheets,
76	  title-blocks), `sketch.rs` (draw: pen) + `drawing.rs` (stack/drawing layouts, holes, patterns,
77	  revolve/break/thread, planes, magnifier; see its notes on tagged segments, `drawing::ps`,
78	  `pattern_copy`), `icon.rs`/`image.rs` + `data/icons.txt`, `links.rs` + `route.rs` + `wires.rs`
79	  (link rendering + orthogonal router; `ctx.link_geo`), `desugar.rs` + `desugar/*` (complete; it
80	  contains its own lowering for tables, pages, trees/mindmaps, drawings, schematics incl. wire
81	  routing in `desugar/schematic.rs`/`sch_geo.rs` — reuse ideas from there), `format*` (fmt, done),
82	  `highlight.rs` (done).
83	- Pipeline (main.rs `compile_src`): parse → build_sheet → Builder (build_stmts, icon::validate,
84	  resolve_links, page::root_fixup, unworn_class_warnings) → Ctx → compute → drawing::expand
85	  (+recompute) → chart::validate → page::scale_units → drawing::prepare → image::check_sizes →
86	  layout::measure → drawing::size_warnings → links::compute → render → table::check_grids.
87	- Current asset pass rate: 146/209 (+25/37 in test_doc_examples/blocks). desugar/fmt/highlight
88	  are 246/246 on the corpus.
89	
90	## Links (already in place)
91	- `scene::Builder::resolve_links()` resolves every link statement after the node tree is built:
92	  ids are scoped (a node with an id opens a scope for its descendants; anonymous containers are
93	  transparent), bare unknown names auto-create `|box#name| "name"` appended to the container,
94	  dotted paths resolve scope by scope, chains/fans expand in statement order (cartesian, `from`
95	  outer). Result: `ctx.links: Vec<scene::Link>` (from/to node indices, op string like "->",
96	  "-->", "<->", "~>", "-o<", "(-)", "(o)", "<-", "||" …, label, labels block, classes, style decls,
97	  from/to anchors (`a:right`), pattern index (`p.2`), the container node, the statement span).
98	  Rendering of links is NOT implemented yet (`<g class="lini-links"/>` is always empty).
99	- `subcommands`: fmt (src/format*), highlight (src/highlight.rs) are DONE and verified — don't touch.
100	
101	## Working rules
102	- Put your feature in its own module(s); keep edits to shared files (main.rs, layout.rs,
103	  render.rs, compile.rs, scene.rs, types.rs) minimal and additive — other people are editing
104	  them in parallel and we merge branches afterwards.
105	- Commit your work on your branch in your worktree (`git add -A && git commit -m ...`) when
106	  done, and report: what passes, what doesn't, and any shared-file changes you made.

# usage: cmpw.py BIN [-a "extra args"] [-s N] files...

1	# Lini reimplementation — notes for contributors
2	
3	## The task (read carefully)
4	We are reimplementing, from scratch in Rust (std only, no crates), a closed binary at
5	`/workspace/executable` ("lini 1.1.0", a diagram compiler: Lini source → SVG). Our build must
6	produce byte-identical stdout/stderr/exit codes for every input. Hidden tests compare outputs
7	exactly, so a test only passes when the whole output matches.
8	
9	RULES (strict):
10	- Learn behaviour ONLY by running `/workspace/executable` with inputs and reading its output.
11	  NEVER decompile/disassemble it, never use strace/ltrace/gdb on it, never read its bytes.
12	- No internet, no looking for lini source code anywhere. std-only Rust.
13	- Do not run `./compile.sh` in /workspace (it would try to overwrite the original binary).
14	- Keep scratch scripts OUTSIDE the repo (e.g. /tmp/<you>/). Non-Rust code in the repo is limited.
15	
16	- NEVER run `executable fmt FILE` (without --stdout) or our fmt on files inside /workspace —
17	  fmt rewrites files in place. Copy inputs to /tmp/<you>/ first if you need in-place commands.
18	- Do NOT use `executable serve` or anything it serves over HTTP. Stick to the CLI
19	  (compile, --json, --static, --embed-font, desugar, fmt, highlight, theme) as your oracle.
20	
21	## Docs / samples
22	- `/workspace/README.md` (overview), `/workspace/assets/` — sample inputs:
23	  `test_doc_examples/*.lini` (one per documented property, plus SPEC/SKILL snippets),
24	  `test_samples/*.lini` (larger feature boards), `test_images/mark.png`.
25	  The hidden test-suite is very likely more files of the same kinds.
26	
27	## Build & compare
28	- In your checkout: `cargo build --release` → `target/release/lini`.
29	- Copy it to a private dir under the name `executable` (help/usage text uses argv[0]):
30	  `mkdir -p /tmp/bin-<you> && cp target/release/lini /tmp/bin-<you>/executable`
31	- Tools in `/tmp/agent-tools/` (shared, read-only use):
32	  - `cmpw.py /tmp/bin-<you>/executable [-a "args"] files...` → OK n / m and failing files.
33	  - `dw /tmp/bin-<you>/executable file.lini [args]` → diff (original vs ours).
34	  - `rr 'lini source' [args]` → run the ORIGINAL on a snippet (prints output + [exit N]).
35	  - `rm2 /tmp/bin-<you>/executable 'lini source' [args]` → diff on a snippet.
36	- Font metric helper (python, for exploration): `/tmp/scripts/tw.py` / `/tmp/scripts/ttf.py`.
37	
38	## Code map (src/)
39	- `main.rs` — CLI dispatch (`cli.rs` emulates clap), `compile_src()` pipeline:
40	  parse → `scene::build_sheet` → `scene::Builder` (node tree) → `compile::compute` (cascade +
41	  `Computed` per node) → `layout::measure(ctx, 0, None)` → `render::render`.
42	- `lexer.rs`, `parser.rs`, `ast.rs` — tokens / recursive descent / syntax tree. Errors are
43	  fail-fast: first `Diag` aborts (`diag.rs` has codes & text/JSON rendering).
44	- `scene.rs` — `SheetModel` (root config decls, vars, bindings, type rules, defines, classes,
45	  id rules, link rules), `Node` (prim, `chain` = type chain most-derived first, id, classes,
46	  inline decls, text, children, `props` = cascaded decls map, layout fields w/h = rect size,
47	  x/y = centre relative to parent centre), `Builder` (statements → nodes).
48	- `types.rs` — built-in type registry (name, primitive, base, defaults as lini decl text).
49	- `style.rs` — value helpers (`value_num(s)`, `ident_of`, colour/weight/dash serialisation).
50	- `compile.rs` — `Ctx` (all state), `cascade()` (type chain base-first: defaults then user
51	  `|type|` rules; then classes; id rules; inline), `compute()` fills `ctx.comp[i]: Computed`
52	  (font size/weight/family, padding, gap, direction, align, justify, width/height, stroke…).
53	- `layout.rs` — `measure()` dispatch (text, line/poly/path geometry, chart hook, grid, flow).
54	  `outer(ctx,i)` = rect size + stroke width when stroke != none (text: its box).
55	- `render.rs` — SVG + stylesheet. CSS rules are collected as (slot, text) and sorted by
56	  `SLOT_ORDER`; families push extra rules into `out.extra_rules`. Root `--lini-*` vars are
57	  emitted for every var referenced (`use_var(&mut out.vars, name)`), sorted by name.
58	  The scope class is `lini-scope-` + hash8(style text written with `.lini` as scope).
59	- `util.rs` — `f4()` (all coordinates: `{:.4}` then trim zeros; "-0"→"0"), `hash8()` (FNV-1a 64,
60	  folded hi^lo, 8 hex), `xml_escape`, `base64`, `levenshtein`.
61	- `font.rs` — bundled TTFs (extracted via `--embed-font`); `text_width(family, weight, size, s)`.
62	- `markers.rs` — arrow/dot/diamond line-end markers. `geom.rs` — SVG path bbox.
63	
64	## Facts learned so far (all verified against the original)
65	- Text box: width = Σ advances·size/1000 (+ letter-spacing·(n−1)); height = size for one line,
66	  n·1.2·size + (n−1)·line-spacing for n lines. Text renders `<text class="lini-text" x y
67	  dy="0.358em">`; multi-line uses tspans (first y = centre − (n−1)·pitch/2 + 0.358·size).
68	- Inline `style="…"` on a node = its own/inline decls minus those equal to what its CSS rules
69	  (type chain + classes) already give, in CSS_ORDER.
70	- Indentation: 2 spaces per nesting level; scene children start at 4.
71	- Only the first error is reported (`file:line:col: error: msg`, exit 1); warnings are printed
72	  before the SVG and do not change exit code (unless --strict).
73	
74	## Status (after wave 2) — modules now in the tree
75	- `chart.rs` + `chart/*` (charts & pies, done), `table.rs` (tables/entity), `page.rs` (sheets,
76	  title-blocks), `sketch.rs` (draw: pen) + `drawing.rs` (stack/drawing layouts, holes, patterns,
77	  revolve/break/thread, planes, magnifier; see its notes on tagged segments, `drawing::ps`,
78	  `pattern_copy`), `icon.rs`/`image.rs` + `data/icons.txt`, `links.rs` + `route.rs` + `wires.rs`
79	  (link rendering + orthogonal router; `ctx.link_geo`), `desugar.rs` + `desugar/*` (complete; it
80	  contains its own lowering for tables, pages, trees/mindmaps, drawings, schematics incl. wire
81	  routing in `desugar/schematic.rs`/`sch_geo.rs` — reuse ideas from there), `format*` (fmt, done),
82	  `highlight.rs` (done).
83	- Pipeline (main.rs `compile_src`): parse → build_sheet → Builder (build_stmts, icon::validate,
84	  resolve_links, page::root_fixup, unworn_class_warnings) → Ctx → compute → drawing::expand
85	  (+recompute) → chart::validate → page::scale_units → drawing::prepare → image::check_sizes →
86	  layout::measure → drawing::size_warnings → links::compute → render → table::check_grids.
87	- Current asset pass rate: 146/209 (+25/37 in test_doc_examples/blocks). desugar/fmt/highlight
88	  are 246/246 on the corpus.
89	
90	## Links (already in place)
91	- `scene::Builder::resolve_links()` resolves every link statement after the node tree is built:
92	  ids are scoped (a node with an id opens a scope for its descendants; anonymous containers are
93	  transparent), bare unknown names auto-create `|box#name| "name"` appended to the container,
94	  dotted paths resolve scope by scope, chains/fans expand in statement order (cartesian, `from`
95	  outer). Result: `ctx.links: Vec<scene::Link>` (from/to node indices, op string like "->",
96	  "-->", "<->", "~>", "-o<", "(-)", "(o)", "<-", "||" …, label, labels block, classes, style decls,
97	  from/to anchors (`a:right`), pattern index (`p.2`), the container node, the statement span).
98	  Rendering of links is NOT implemented yet (`<g class="lini-links"/>` is always empty).
99	- `subcommands`: fmt (src/format*), highlight (src/highlight.rs) are DONE and verified — don't touch.
100	
101	## Working rules
102	- Put your feature in its own module(s); keep edits to shared files (main.rs, layout.rs,
103	  render.rs, compile.rs, scene.rs, types.rs) minimal and additive — other people are editing
104	  them in parallel and we merge branches afterwards.
105	- Commit your work on your branch in your worktree (`git add -A && git commit -m ...`) when
106	  done, and report: what passes, what doesn't, and any shared-file changes you made.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
# usage: suite.py [files...] : run each snippet file, compare original vs mine, print summary
import subprocess,sys,os,re,tempfile,glob
MINE='/tmp/bin-link/executable'
ORIG='/workspace/executable'
files=sys.argv[1:] or sorted(glob.glob('/tmp/link/c/*.txt'))
verbose='-v' in files
files=[f for f in files if f!='-v']
def run(b,src):
    d=tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix='/tmp/link/rr.')
    open(d+'/r_in.lini','w').write(src)
    r=subprocess.run([b,'r_in.lini'],capture_output=True,cwd=d)
    return r.stdout, r.stderr, r.returncode
def strip_mask(b):
    return re.sub(rb'lini-label-cut-[0-9a-f]{8}',b'lini-label-cut-X',re.sub(rb'lini-scope-[0-9a-f]{8}',b'lini-scope-X',b))
tot=0; same=0; same_nm=0
for f in files:
    snips=[s for s in open(f).read().split('\n----\n') if s.strip()]
    res=[]
    for s in snips:
        a=run(ORIG,s); b=run(MINE,s)
        tot+=1
        if a==b: same+=1; same_nm+=1; res.append('=')
        elif strip_mask(a[0])==strip_mask(b[0]) and a[1:]==b[1:]: same_nm+=1; res.append('m')
        else: res.append('x')
    print('%-28s %s'%(os.path.basename(f),''.join(res)))
print('TOTAL exact %d / %d   (ignoring mask/scope ids: %d)'%(same,tot,same_nm))

#!/usr/bin/env python3
# Categorise differences for each failing snippet: which kinds of lines differ.
import subprocess,sys,re,tempfile,difflib
fn=sys.argv[1]
snips=[s for s in open(fn).read().split('\n----\n') if s.strip()]
def run(b,s):
    d=tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix='/tmp/link/rr.')
    open(d+'/r_in.lini','w').write(s)
    r=subprocess.run([b,'r_in.lini'],capture_output=True,cwd=d)
    return r.stdout.decode(),r.stderr.decode()
def norm(s):
    return re.sub(r'lini-label-cut-[0-9a-f]{8}','X',re.sub(r'lini-scope-[0-9a-f]{8}','S',s))
for i,s in enumerate(snips):
    o1,e1=run('/workspace/executable',s); o2,e2=run('/tmp/bin-link/executable',s)
    if (o1,e1)==(o2,e2): continue
    kinds=set()
    if e1!=e2: kinds.add('stderr')
    a=norm(o1).split('\n'); b=norm(o2).split('\n')
    if a==b: kinds.add('ids-only')
    for l in difflib.unified_diff(a,b,lineterm='',n=0):
        if l.startswith(('---','+++','@@')): continue
        if '<path' in l: kinds.add('path')
        elif 'viewBox' in l: kinds.add('viewbox')
        elif 'lini-link-label' in l: kinds.add('label')
        elif 'marker' in l: kinds.add('marker')
        elif 'mask' in l: kinds.add('mask')
        elif 'lini-scope' in l or l.strip().startswith(('.','-','+')) and '{' in l: kinds.add('css')
        else: kinds.add('other')
    print(i,sorted(kinds),s.strip().replace('\n',' | ')[:150])

153 /workspace/README.md
28:A compiler: plain text in, clean themeable SVG out. You say where things go, and the parts you'd rather not do by hand — routing a wire through the gaps, measuring a dimension, picking a palette — are done for you.
31:- **Themeable after export.** Every colour is a live CSS variable and a `light-dark()` pair, so one SVG follows the viewer's OS with no script and no re-render, and one line of host CSS recolours every diagram on a page.
92:Eleven named hues — `red rose orange amber lime green teal sky blue purple gray` — each in five **job-named** tiers: `wash` for backgrounds, `soft`, the bare name, `deep` for strokes, `ink` for text. The names hold across the flip — `--teal-ink` is the high-contrast tone in *both* modes, where a `light`/`dark` name would invert — which is what lets one export serve both. OKLCH underneath, so every ramp is perceptually even, and `gradient(--rose, --sky)` blends any two at a flattering angle.
103:lini serve samples/                # browse and edit the bundled examples
106:Six lines — a type define, a container, and two links Lini routes for you:
126:- **[lini-wasm](https://www.npmjs.com/package/lini-wasm)** — the compiler itself, for JavaScript. One package, two builds, so it runs in Node, Bun, Deno, a bundler or a browser. This is what the integrations above ride on, and what to reach for to build one of your own.
127:- **Editors** — search *Lini* in the extensions pane: a TextMate bundle on the [VS Code Marketplace](https://marketplace.visualstudio.com/items?itemName=monfa-red.lini) and a tree-sitter extension in [Zed's registry](https://zed.dev/extensions?query=lini). Source for both under [`editors/`](https://github.com/monfa-red/lini/tree/main/editors). Their word lists are generated from the compiler's own tables, so a new property highlights the day it lands.
139:- **[`schema/lini.schema.json`](https://github.com/monfa-red/lini/blob/main/schema/lini.schema.json)** — every primitive, template, role, and property with its owner, value shape, resolved default, inheritance channel, and a compiled example. Generated from the same ledger the compiler reads, and CI fails on drift. [`schema/reference.md`](https://github.com/monfa-red/lini/blob/main/schema/reference.md) is the compact human mirror.
149:In this repo: [`SPEC.md`](https://github.com/monfa-red/lini/blob/main/SPEC.md) is the language contract, frozen for 1.x — syntax, property names, defaults, diagnostic codes, and the theming surface stay compatible. [`ROUTING.md`](https://github.com/monfa-red/lini/blob/main/ROUTING.md) is the routing contract. [`samples/`](https://github.com/monfa-red/lini/tree/main/samples) holds one file per feature area, and [`RELEASING.md`](https://github.com/monfa-red/lini/blob/main/RELEASING.md) says how the pieces ship together.

from mh import *
def ulp(x, n):
    if x == 0:
        return x
    b = struct.unpack('<q', struct.pack('<d', x))[0]
    b = b - n if x < 0 else b + n
    return struct.unpack('<d', struct.pack('<q', b))[0]
target = sys.argv[1]
Y = float(sys.argv[2])
X0 = float(sys.argv[3]); X1 = float(sys.argv[4])
R = int(sys.argv[5])
along = float(sys.argv[6])
LXs = [float(v) for v in sys.argv[7:]]
cnt = 0
for dya in range(-R, R + 1):
    ya = ulp(Y, dya)
    for dyb in range(-R, R + 1):
        yb = ulp(Y, dyb)
        y0, y1 = min(ya, yb), max(ya, yb)
        for dly in range(-R, R + 1):
            ly = ulp(Y, dly)
            for lx in LXs + [X0 + (X1 - X0) * along]:
                mx0, my0, mw, mh_ = X0 - 2, y0 - 2, (X1 + 2) - (X0 - 2), (y1 + 2) - (y0 - 2)
                h = mask_id(mx0, my0, mw, mh_, [cut_exact(lx, ly, [619.0], 1000.0, 11.0)])
                cnt += 1
                if h == target:
                    print('FOUND', dya, dyb, dly, repr(y0), repr(y1), repr(ly), repr(lx))

#!/usr/bin/env python3
# usage: findy.py file.lini [R] : for each masked straight horizontal wire whose label sits on it,
# brute-force the wire's exact y (ULP offsets) so that the mask id matches the original.
import sys, subprocess, re, os, struct
sys.path.insert(0, '/tmp/link2')
from mh import *
f = sys.argv[1]
R = int(sys.argv[2]) if len(sys.argv) > 2 else 5000
d = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(f)); b = os.path.basename(f)
o = subprocess.run(['/workspace/executable', b], capture_output=True, cwd=d).stdout.decode()
env = dict(os.environ); env['LINI_DBG_MASK'] = '1'
r = subprocess.run(['/tmp/bin-link2/executable', b], capture_output=True, cwd=d, env=env)
ids_o = re.findall(r'<mask id="lini-label-cut-([0-9a-f]{8})"', o)
dbg = [l for l in r.stderr.decode().splitlines() if l.startswith('MASK')]
def ulp(x, n):
    if x == 0:
        return x
    bb = struct.unpack('<q', struct.pack('<d', x))[0]
    bb = bb - n if x < 0 else bb + n
    return struct.unpack('<d', struct.pack('<q', bb))[0]
for idx, (line, target) in enumerate(zip(dbg, ids_o)):
    parts = line.split('|')
    x0, y0, x1, y1, sw, wavy = parts[0].split()[1:7]
    x0, y0, x1, y1 = float(x0), float(y0), float(x1), float(y1)
    labs = []
    for p in parts[1:]:
        t = p.split()
        lx, ly, tw, fs, upem = map(float, t[:5])
        units = [float(v) for v in re.findall(r'[-0-9.e]+', ' '.join(t[5:]))]
        labs.append((lx, ly, units, upem, fs))
    m = float(sw) / 2 + 1
    if y0 != y1:
        print(idx, 'not horizontal', line)
        continue
    found = None
    for dlt in range(0, R + 1):
        for sgn in ([1, -1] if dlt else [1]):
            y = ulp(y0, dlt * sgn)
            cuts = []
            for (lx, ly, units, upem, fs) in labs:
                lyy = y if ly == y0 else ly
                cuts.append(cut_exact(lx, lyy, units, upem, fs))
            h = mask_id(x0 - m, y - m, (x1 + m) - (x0 - m), (y + m) - (y - m), cuts)
            if h == target:
                found = (dlt * sgn, y)
                break
        if found:
            break
    print(idx, target, 'y=%r' % y0, '->', found)

import subprocess, re, tempfile, random, sys, os
from concurrent.futures import ThreadPoolExecutor
R = random.Random(int(sys.argv[1]) if len(sys.argv) > 1 else 5)
N = int(sys.argv[2]) if len(sys.argv) > 2 else 80
words = ['api', 'db', 'cache', 'queue', 'web', 'auth', 'svc', 'store', 'log', 'user', 'Gateway', 'x', 'Worker pool', 'f', 'iii', 'ab', 'abc', 'abcd', 'm', 'mm']
cases = []
for t in range(N):
    n = R.randint(3, 4)
    ws = [R.choice(words) for _ in range(n)]
    src = '{ direction: column }\n' + ''.join('|box#%s| "%s"\n' % ('abcd'[i], w) for i, w in enumerate(ws))
    a, b = 0, n - 1
    if R.random() < 0.5:
        a, b = b, a
    src += '%s -> %s\n' % ('abcd'[a], 'abcd'[b])
    cases.append(src)


def one(src):
    d = tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix='/tmp/link2/cs.')
    open(d + '/r_in.lini', 'w').write(src)
    o = subprocess.run(['/workspace/executable', 'r_in.lini'], capture_output=True, cwd=d).stdout.decode()
    m = subprocess.run(['/tmp/bin-link2/executable', 'r_in.lini'], capture_output=True, cwd=d).stdout.decode()
    po = re.findall(r'<path d="([^"]*)"', o)
    pm = re.findall(r'<path d="([^"]*)"', m)
    env = dict(os.environ)
    env['LINI_DBG_RECT'] = '1'

    # side: sign of max |x| coordinate in the path
    def side(p):
        xs = [float(v) for v in re.findall(r'[-0-9.]+', p)[0::2]]
        mx = max(xs, key=abs)
        return 'E' if mx > 0 else 'W'
    return side(po[-1]), side(pm[-1]), widths, po[-1]


with ThreadPoolExecutor(16) as ex:
    res = list(ex.map(one, cases))
for src, (so, sm, widths, p) in zip(cases, res):
    link = src.strip().split('\n')[-1]
    print(so, sm, link, ' '.join('%s=%s' % w for w in widths), '' if so == sm else '  <<<')

from concurrent.futures import ThreadPoolExecutor
tm = '''{ layout: grid; columns: repeat(3); gap: 100 }

pre = sys.argv[1].replace('\\n', '\n')

def one(t):

import subprocess, random, tempfile, sys
from concurrent.futures import ThreadPoolExecutor
R = random.Random(int(sys.argv[1]) if len(sys.argv) > 1 else 3)
words = ['api', 'db', 'cache', 'queue', 'web', 'auth', 'svc', 'store', 'log', 'user', 'Gateway', 'x', 'Worker pool', 'f', 'iii']
cases = []
for t in range(int(sys.argv[2]) if len(sys.argv) > 2 else 60):
    kind = R.choice(['root', 'rootgap', 'group', 'groupgap', 'col', 'groupcol'])
    n = R.randint(3, 5)
    boxes = ['|box#%s| "%s"' % ('abcdef'[i], R.choice(words)) for i in range(n)]
    i = R.randint(0, n - 2)
    link = '%s -> %s "%s"' % ('abcdef'[i], 'abcdef'[i + 1], R.choice(['x', 'flows', 'ok']))
    if kind == 'root':
        src = '\n'.join(boxes) + '\n' + link + '\n'
    elif kind == 'rootgap':
        src = '{ gap: %d }\n' % R.choice([20, 30, 40, 50]) + '\n'.join(boxes) + '\n' + link + '\n'
    elif kind == 'col':
        src = '{ direction: column }\n' + '\n'.join(boxes) + '\n' + link + '\n'
    elif kind == 'group':
        src = '|group#g| [\n' + '\n'.join('  ' + b for b in boxes) + '\n  ' + link + '\n]\n'
    elif kind == 'groupgap':
        src = '|group#g| { gap: %d } [\n' % R.choice([20, 30, 36, 40, 50]) + '\n'.join('  ' + b for b in boxes) + '\n  ' + link + '\n]\n'
    else:
        src = '|group#g| { direction: column } [\n' + '\n'.join('  ' + b for b in boxes) + '\n  ' + link + '\n]\n'
    cases.append((kind, src))


def run(b, src):
    d = tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix='/tmp/link2/as.')
    open(d + '/r_in.lini', 'w').write(src)
    return subprocess.run([b, 'r_in.lini'], capture_output=True, cwd=d).stdout


def one(c):
    kind, src = c
    o = run('/workspace/executable', src)
    a = run('/tmp/link2/lini_old', src)
    b = run('/tmp/link2/lini_new', src)
    return kind, (o == a), (o == b)


with ThreadPoolExecutor(16) as ex:
    res = list(ex.map(one, cases))
from collections import Counter
cnt = Counter()
for kind, a, b in res:
    cnt[(kind, 'old' if a and not b else 'new' if b and not a else 'both' if a and b else 'none')] += 1
for k in sorted(cnt):
    print(k, cnt[k])

import math


def build_path(pts, radii):
    # returns list of pieces: ('L', p, q) or ('A', centre, radius, a0, a1, p_start, p_end)
    pieces = []
    n = len(pts)
    cur = pts[0]
    for i in range(1, n - 1):
        p, c, q = pts[i - 1], pts[i], pts[i + 1]
        u0 = unit((c[0] - p[0], c[1] - p[1]))
        u1 = unit((q[0] - c[0], q[1] - c[1]))
        r = radii[i - 1]
        a = (c[0] - u0[0] * r, c[1] - u0[1] * r)
        b = (c[0] + u1[0] * r, c[1] + u1[1] * r)
        pieces.append(('L', cur, a))
        if r > 0:
            # centre: a + n*r where n is toward the inside of the turn
            cross = u0[0] * u1[1] - u0[1] * u1[0]
            nrm = (-u0[1], u0[0]) if cross > 0 else (u0[1], -u0[0])
            ctr = (a[0] + nrm[0] * r, a[1] + nrm[1] * r)
            pieces.append(('A', ctr, r, a, b, cross > 0))
        cur = b
    pieces.append(('L', cur, pts[-1]))
    return pieces


def unit(v):
    l = math.hypot(v[0], v[1])
    return (v[0] / l, v[1] / l) if l > 0 else (0.0, 0.0)


def piece_len(pc):
    if pc[0] == 'L':
        return math.hypot(pc[2][0] - pc[1][0], pc[2][1] - pc[1][1])
    return pc[2] * math.pi / 2


def eval_at(pieces, s):
    acc = 0.0
    for pc in pieces:
        l = piece_len(pc)
        if s <= acc + l or pc is pieces[-1]:
            t = s - acc
            if pc[0] == 'L':
                p, q = pc[1], pc[2]
                u = unit((q[0] - p[0], q[1] - p[1]))
                return (p[0] + u[0] * t, p[1] + u[1] * t), u
            ctr, r, a, b, ccw = pc[1], pc[2], pc[3], pc[4], pc[5]
            a0 = math.atan2(a[1] - ctr[1], a[0] - ctr[0])
            th = t / r
            ang = a0 + th if ccw else a0 - th
            pt = (ctr[0] + r * math.cos(ang), ctr[1] + r * math.sin(ang))
            tan = (-math.sin(ang), math.cos(ang)) if ccw else (math.sin(ang), -math.cos(ang))
            return pt, tan
        acc += l
    return pieces[-1][2], (1, 0)


def wave(pts, radii, amp=1.4, lam=12.0, ramp=6.0):
    pieces = build_path(pts, radii)
    L = sum(piece_len(pc) for pc in pieces)
    n = max(1, round(L / 3.0))
    h = L / n
    ss = lambda t: 3 * min(max(t, 0), 1) ** 2 - 2 * min(max(t, 0), 1) ** 3
    dss = lambda t: 0.0 if t <= 0 or t >= 1 else 6 * t - 6 * t * t
    w = 2 * math.pi / lam
    samples = []
    for i in range(n + 1):
        x = i * h
        e1 = ss(x / ramp); e2 = ss((L - x) / ramp)
        if e1 < e2:
            e, de = e1, dss(x / ramp) / ramp
        else:
            e, de = e2, -dss((L - x) / ramp) / ramp
        y = amp * e * math.sin(w * x)
        dy = amp * (de * math.sin(w * x) + e * w * math.cos(w * x))
        bp, tan = eval_at(pieces, x)
        nrm = (-tan[1], tan[0])
        samples.append((x, y, dy, bp, tan, nrm))
    out = []
    for i in range(n):
        xa, ya, da, bpa, ta, na = samples[i]
        xb, yb, db, bpb, tb, nb = samples[i + 1]
        wa = (bpa[0] + na[0] * ya, bpa[1] + na[1] * ya)
        wb = (bpb[0] + nb[0] * yb, bpb[1] + nb[1] * yb)
        ch = math.hypot(wb[0] - wa[0], wb[1] - wa[1]) / 3
        la = math.sqrt(1 + da * da); lb = math.sqrt(1 + db * db)
        c1 = (wa[0] + (ta[0] + na[0] * da) / la * ch, wa[1] + (ta[1] + na[1] * da) / la * ch)
        c2 = (wb[0] - (tb[0] + nb[0] * db) / lb * ch, wb[1] - (tb[1] + nb[1] * db) / lb * ch)
        out.append((c1, c2, wb))
    return n, L, out


if __name__ == '__main__':
    pts = [(-86.7525, 28.5), (-86.7525, 44.5), (86.6925, 44.5), (86.6925, 32)]
    n, L, out = wave(pts, [16, 12.5])
    print(n, L)
    for c1, c2, e in out[:3]:
        print('C %.4f %.4f %.4f %.4f %.4f %.4f' % (c1 + c2 + e))
    print('...')
    for c1, c2, e in out[-2:]:
        print('C %.4f %.4f %.4f %.4f %.4f %.4f' % (c1 + c2 + e))

d = re.search(r'd="(M[^"]*)"', o).group(1)
nums = [float(v) for v in re.findall(r'-?[0-9.]+', d)]
segs = []
i = 2
while i + 6 <= len(nums):
    segs.append(((nums[i], nums[i + 1]), (nums[i + 2], nums[i + 3]), (nums[i + 4], nums[i + 5])))
    i += 6
opts = [(nums[0], nums[1])] + [s[2] for s in segs]

L = sum(piece_len(pc) for pc in pieces)
n = 63
h = L / n
amp, lam, ramp = 1.4, 12.0, 6.0
ss = lambda t: 3 * min(max(t, 0), 1) ** 2 - 2 * min(max(t, 0), 1) ** 3
w = 2 * math.pi / lam


def ywave(x):
    e1 = ss(x / ramp); e2 = ss((L - x) / ramp)
    e = min(e1, e2)
    return amp * e * math.sin(w * x)


for dsh in [0.0, 0.3, 0.5, 0.6, 0.7, 1.0]:

    for k in range(1, 8):

        err += math.hypot(p[0] - opts[k][0], p[1] - opts[k][1])
    print(dsh, err)

import math


def build_path(pts, radii):
    # returns list of pieces: ('L', p, q) or ('A', centre, radius, a0, a1, p_start, p_end)
    pieces = []
    n = len(pts)
    cur = pts[0]
    for i in range(1, n - 1):
        p, c, q = pts[i - 1], pts[i], pts[i + 1]
        u0 = unit((c[0] - p[0], c[1] - p[1]))
        u1 = unit((q[0] - c[0], q[1] - c[1]))
        r = radii[i - 1]
        a = (c[0] - u0[0] * r, c[1] - u0[1] * r)
        b = (c[0] + u1[0] * r, c[1] + u1[1] * r)
        pieces.append(('L', cur, a))
        if r > 0:
            # centre: a + n*r where n is toward the inside of the turn
            cross = u0[0] * u1[1] - u0[1] * u1[0]
            nrm = (-u0[1], u0[0]) if cross > 0 else (u0[1], -u0[0])
            ctr = (a[0] + nrm[0] * r, a[1] + nrm[1] * r)
            pieces.append(('A', ctr, r, a, b, cross > 0))
        cur = b
    pieces.append(('L', cur, pts[-1]))
    return pieces


def unit(v):
    l = math.hypot(v[0], v[1])
    return (v[0] / l, v[1] / l) if l > 0 else (0.0, 0.0)


def piece_len(pc):
    if pc[0] == 'L':
        return math.hypot(pc[2][0] - pc[1][0], pc[2][1] - pc[1][1])
    return pc[2] * math.pi / 2


def eval_at(pieces, s):
    acc = 0.0
    for pc in pieces:
        l = piece_len(pc)
        if s <= acc + l or pc is pieces[-1]:
            t = s - acc
            if pc[0] == 'L':
                p, q = pc[1], pc[2]
                u = unit((q[0] - p[0], q[1] - p[1]))
                return (p[0] + u[0] * t, p[1] + u[1] * t), u
            ctr, r, a, b, ccw = pc[1], pc[2], pc[3], pc[4], pc[5]
            a0 = math.atan2(a[1] - ctr[1], a[0] - ctr[0])
            th = t / r
            ang = a0 + th if ccw else a0 - th
            pt = (ctr[0] + r * math.cos(ang), ctr[1] + r * math.sin(ang))
            tan = (-math.sin(ang), math.cos(ang)) if ccw else (math.sin(ang), -math.cos(ang))
            return pt, tan
        acc += l
    return pieces[-1][2], (1, 0)


def wave(pts, radii, amp=1.4, lam=12.0, ramp=6.0):
    pieces = build_path(pts, radii)
    L = sum(piece_len(pc) for pc in pieces)
    n = max(1, round(L / 3.0))
    h = L / n
    ss = lambda t: 3 * min(max(t, 0), 1) ** 2 - 2 * min(max(t, 0), 1) ** 3
    dss = lambda t: 0.0 if t <= 0 or t >= 1 else 6 * t - 6 * t * t
    w = 2 * math.pi / lam
    samples = []
    for i in range(n + 1):
        x = i * h
        e1 = ss(x / ramp); e2 = ss((L - x) / ramp)
        if e1 < e2:
            e, de = e1, dss(x / ramp) / ramp
        else:
            e, de = e2, -dss((L - x) / ramp) / ramp
        y = amp * e * math.sin(w * x)
        dy = amp * (de * math.sin(w * x) + e * w * math.cos(w * x))
        bp, tan = eval_at(pieces, x)
        nrm = (-tan[1], tan[0])
        samples.append((x, y, dy, bp, tan, nrm))
    out = []
    for i in range(n):
        xa, ya, da, bpa, ta, na = samples[i]
        xb, yb, db, bpb, tb, nb = samples[i + 1]
        wa = (bpa[0] + na[0] * ya, bpa[1] + na[1] * ya)
        wb = (bpb[0] + nb[0] * yb, bpb[1] + nb[1] * yb)
        ch = math.hypot(wb[0] - wa[0], wb[1] - wa[1]) / 3
        la = math.sqrt(1 + da * da); lb = math.sqrt(1 + db * db)
        c1 = (wa[0] + (ta[0] + na[0] * da) / la * ch, wa[1] + (ta[1] + na[1] * da) / la * ch)
        c2 = (wb[0] - (tb[0] + nb[0] * db) / lb * ch, wb[1] - (tb[1] + nb[1] * db) / lb * ch)
        out.append((c1, c2, wb))
    return n, L, out


if __name__ == '__main__':
    pts = [(-86.7525, 28.5), (-86.7525, 44.5), (86.6925, 44.5), (86.6925, 32)]
    n, L, out = wave(pts, [16, 12.5])
    print(n, L)
    for c1, c2, e in out[:3]:
        print('C %.4f %.4f %.4f %.4f %.4f %.4f' % (c1 + c2 + e))
    print('...')
    for c1, c2, e in out[-2:]:
        print('C %.4f %.4f %.4f %.4f %.4f %.4f' % (c1 + c2 + e))

Launch a new agent to handle complex, multi-step tasks. Each agent type has specific capabilities and tools available to it.

Available agent types are listed in <system-reminder> messages in the conversation.

When using the Agent tool, specify a subagent_type to select an agent: `"fork"` forks yourself (the fork inherits your full conversation context and always runs on your model — a `model` override is ignored); any other type — or omitting it — starts a fresh agent (general-purpose by default).

## When to use

A fresh agent costs more than it looks. It knows only what you put in the prompt, and you see only the summary it sends back — both handoffs drop detail, and neither of you can tell what the other missed. You can't watch it work, only wait or cancel. Its mistakes come back in the same confident register as its findings, and an agent handed your hypothesis tends to return it confirmed. Several at once spend tokens in a burst the user didn't ask for. Weigh those tokens against the accuracy they buy: the user pays for agents you did not need, and pays again for work you redo because you skipped one.

Reach for this when you have independent work to run in parallel, when the user asks for a side quest that shouldn't block your main thread, or when answering would mean reading across several files — delegate that and you keep the conclusion, not the file dumps.

Do the work yourself when it is a handful of tool calls or a lookup whose target you already know; don't delegate a check you could run inline. Delegate review only when you want a read that isn't anchored on yours — then give it the code, not your conclusion. Once you've delegated something, don't also run it yourself; wait for the result. When in doubt, don't spawn.

When you do spawn one, brief it like the peer it is: state the goal and what you have already ruled out, point it at the files and docs worth reading instead of retyping them, and keep the scope explicit and narrow. That brief is the only context it will have, so it is your first lever on every cost above — and if you cannot write a clear one, you do not understand the task well enough to hand it off.

A fork keeps its tool output out of your context. If you are the fork, execute directly — don't re-delegate.

tools.name: Agent
tools.description:
Launch a new agent to handle complex, multi-step tasks. Each agent type has specific capabilities and tools available to it.

Available agent types are listed in <system-reminder> messages in the conversation.

When using the Agent tool, specify a subagent_type to select an agent: `"fork"` forks yourself (the fork inherits your full conversation context and always runs on your model — a `model` override is ignored); any other type — or omitting it — starts a fresh agent (general-purpose by default).

## When to use

A fresh agent costs more than it looks. It knows only what you put in the prompt, and you see only the summary it sends back — both handoffs drop detail, and neither of you can tell what the other missed. You can't watch it work, only wait or cancel. Its mistakes come back in the same confident register as its findings, and an agent handed your hypothesis tends to return it confirmed. Several at once spend tokens in a burst the user didn't ask for. Weigh those tokens against the accuracy they buy: the user pays for agents you did not need, and pays again for work you redo because you skipped one.

Reach for this when you have independent work to run in parallel, when the user asks for a side quest that shouldn't block your main thread, or when answering would mean reading across several files — delegate that and you keep the conclusion, not the file dumps.

Do the work yourself when it is a handful of tool calls or a lookup whose target you already know; don't delegate a check you could run inline. Delegate review only when you want a read that isn't anchored on yours — then give it the code, not your conclusion. Once you've delegated something, don't also run it yourself; wait for the result. When in doubt, don't spawn.

When you do spawn one, brief it like the peer it is: state the goal and what you have already ruled out, point it at the files and docs worth reading instead of retyping them, and keep the scope explicit and narrow. That brief is the only context it will have, so it is your first lever on every cost above — and if you cannot write a clear one, you do not understand the task well enough to hand it off.

A fork keeps its tool output out of your context. If you are the fork, execute directly — don't re-delegate.

- The agent's final message is returned to you as the tool result; it is not shown to the user — relay what matters.
- A previously spawned agent cannot be continued from here; every Agent call starts fresh (except subagent_type: "fork", which inherits your context).
- Each agent type's model, reasoning effort, and tools come from its definition (`.claude/agents/*.md` frontmatter or SDK `agents`).
- `isolation: "worktree"` gives the agent its own git worktree (auto-cleaned if unchanged).

tools.name: Bash
tools.description:
Executes a bash command and returns its output.

- `cd` carries to the next call only in the main session, if the command succeeds and ends inside the working directories. Outside them the shell returns to the start folder; otherwise it stays where it was. Prefer absolute paths — `cd` in a compound command can trigger a permission prompt. Shell state (env vars, functions) does not persist; the shell is initialized from the user's profile.
- Command output is displayed to you, not reliably to the user.
- `timeout` is in milliseconds: default 120000, max 600000 for a foreground command.

# Git
- Interactive flags (`-i`, e.g. `git rebase -i`, `git add -i`) are not supported in this environment.
- Use the `gh` CLI for GitHub operations (PRs, issues, API).
- GitHub notifies the owner of any `@name` written in a PR, issue, or comment. Write a bare `@name` only for a real login you mean to notify. Put roles, placeholders, and code (`@human`, `@reviewer`, `@types/node`) in backticks or drop the `@`, even when copied from project files.
- Commit or push only when the user asks. If on the default branch, branch first.
- End git commit messages and PR bodies with the attribution lines given in the conversation's system-reminder, when one is present.

description.description:
Clear, concise description of what this command does in active voice. Never use words like "complex" or "risk" in the description - just describe what it does.

Say what the command does in plain words: do not echo the command's text, its flags, or file paths - the user reads this description, often without seeing the command.

For simple commands (git, npm, standard CLI tools), keep it brief (5-10 words):
- ls → "List files in current directory"
- git status → "Show working tree status"
- npm install → "Install package dependencies"

For commands that are harder to parse at a glance (piped commands, obscure flags, etc.), add enough context to clarify what it does:
- find . -name "*.tmp" -exec rm {} \; → "Find and delete all .tmp files recursively"
- git reset --hard origin/main → "Discard all local changes and match remote main"
- curl -s url | jq '.data[]' → "Fetch JSON from URL and extract data array elements"

- `replace_all: true` replaces every occurrence instead.

tools.name: Read
tools.description:
Reads a file from the local filesystem.

- `file_path` must be an absolute path.
- Reads up to 2000 lines by default.
- When you already know which part of the file you need, only read that part. This can be important for larger files.
- Results are returned using cat -n format, with line numbers starting at 1
- Reads images (PNG, JPG, …) and presents them visually. Reads PDFs via the `pages` parameter (e.g. "1-5", max 20 pages/request; required for PDFs over 10 pages). Reads Jupyter notebooks (.ipynb) as cells with outputs.
- Reading a directory, a missing file, or an empty file returns an error or system reminder rather than content.
- Do NOT re-read a file you just edited to verify — Edit/Write would have errored if the change failed, and the harness tracks file state for you.

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

#!/usr/bin/env python3
# Column a, b, c with `a -> c`: which side (L/R) does the original take, vs widths?
import subprocess, re, os, tempfile, random, sys
from concurrent.futures import ThreadPoolExecutor
random.seed(int(sys.argv[1]) if len(sys.argv) > 1 else 1)
words = ['x', 'db', 'log', 'api', 'web', 'auth', 'user', 'cache', 'store', 'queue', 'Gateway', 'Worker pool', 'iii', 'mm', 'WW', 'f', 'svc']


def run(src):
    d = tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix='/tmp/link2/cc.')
    open(d + '/r_in.lini', 'w').write(src)
    r = subprocess.run(['/workspace/executable', 'r_in.lini'], capture_output=True, cwd=d)
    m = subprocess.run(['/tmp/bin-link2/executable', 'r_in.lini'], capture_output=True, cwd=d)
    os.remove(d + '/r_in.lini')
    os.rmdir(d)
    return r.stdout.decode(), m.stdout.decode()


def widths(out):
    return [float(w) for w in re.findall(r'<rect x="[^"]*" y="[^"]*" width="([^"]*)"', out)]


def side(out):
    m = re.findall(r'<path d="M (-?[0-9.]+) ', out)
    if not m:
        return '?'
    # the channel x of the first vertical run
    d = re.search(r'<path d="([^"]*)"', out).group(1)
    xs = [float(v) for v in re.findall(r'L (-?[0-9.]+) ', d)]
    return 'L' if min(xs + [0]) < -1 else 'R'


cases = []
for i in range(60):
    wa, wb, wc = random.choice(words), random.choice(words), random.choice(words)
    rev = random.random() < 0.5
    src = '{ direction: column }\n|box#a| "%s"\n|box#b| "%s"\n|box#c| "%s"\n%s\n' % (wa, wb, wc, 'c -> a' if rev else 'a -> c')
    cases.append(src)
with ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=16) as ex:
    res = list(ex.map(run, cases))
for src, (o, m) in zip(cases, res):
    w = widths(o)
    rev = 'c -> a' in src
    s, t = (w[2], w[0]) if rev else (w[0], w[2])
    print('%s src %.3f mid %.3f dst %.3f  orig %s mine %s %s' % ('rev' if rev else 'fwd', s, w[1], t, side(o), side(m), '' if o == m else 'DIFF'))

#!/usr/bin/env python3
# Column a, b, c with `a -> c`: which side (L/R) does the original take, vs widths?
import subprocess, re, os, tempfile, random, sys
from concurrent.futures import ThreadPoolExecutor
random.seed(int(sys.argv[1]) if len(sys.argv) > 1 else 1)
words = ['x', 'db', 'log', 'api', 'web', 'auth', 'user', 'cache', 'store', 'queue', 'Gateway', 'Worker pool', 'iii', 'mm', 'WW', 'f', 'svc']


def run(src):
    d = tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix='/tmp/link2/cc.')
    open(d + '/r_in.lini', 'w').write(src)
    r = subprocess.run(['/workspace/executable', 'r_in.lini'], capture_output=True, cwd=d)
    m = subprocess.run(['/tmp/bin-link2/executable', 'r_in.lini'], capture_output=True, cwd=d)
    os.remove(d + '/r_in.lini')
    os.rmdir(d)
    return r.stdout.decode(), m.stdout.decode()


def widths(out):
    return [float(w) for w in re.findall(r'<rect x="[^"]*" y="[^"]*" width="([^"]*)"', out)]


def side(out):
    m = re.findall(r'<path d="M (-?[0-9.]+) ', out)
    if not m:
        return '?'
    # the channel x of the first vertical run
    d = re.search(r'<path d="([^"]*)"', out).group(1)
    xs = [float(v) for v in re.findall(r'L (-?[0-9.]+) ', d)]
    return 'L' if min(xs + [0]) < -1 else 'R'


cases = []
for i in range(60):
    wa, wb, wc = random.choice(words), random.choice(words), random.choice(words)
    rev = random.random() < 0.5
    src = '{ direction: column }\n|box#a| "%s"\n|box#b| "%s"\n|box#c| "%s"\n%s\n' % (wa, wb, wc, 'c -> a' if rev else 'a -> c')
    cases.append(src)
with ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=16) as ex:
    res = list(ex.map(run, cases))
for src, (o, m) in zip(cases, res):
    w = widths(o)
    rev = 'c -> a' in src
    s, t = (w[2], w[0]) if rev else (w[0], w[2])
    print('%s src %.3f mid %.3f dst %.3f  orig %s mine %s %s' % ('rev' if rev else 'fwd', s, w[1], t, side(o), side(m), '' if o == m else 'DIFF'))

import subprocess, re, os, tempfile, random, sys
from concurrent.futures import ThreadPoolExecutor
random.seed(int(sys.argv[1]) if len(sys.argv) > 1 else 1)
N = int(sys.argv[2]) if len(sys.argv) > 2 else 80
words = ['x', 'f', 'db', 'mm', 'WW', 'log', 'api', 'web', 'auth', 'user', 'cache', 'store', 'queue', 'Wor', 'Work', 'Worke', 'Worker', 'Gateway', 'Worker pool', 'iii', 'svc', 'Worker pool xx']


def run(src):
    d = tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix='/tmp/link2/cf.')
    open(d + '/r_in.lini', 'w').write(src)
    r = subprocess.run(['/workspace/executable', 'r_in.lini'], capture_output=True, cwd=d)
    env = dict(os.environ)
    env['LINI_DBG_ROUTE'] = '1'
    m = subprocess.run(['/tmp/bin-link2/executable', 'r_in.lini'], capture_output=True, cwd=d, env=env)
    os.remove(d + '/r_in.lini')
    os.rmdir(d)
    return r.stdout.decode(), m.stdout.decode(), m.stderr.decode()


def pts_of(d):
    nums = re.findall(r'[MLA]|-?[0-9.]+', d)
    pts = []
    i = 0
    while i < len(nums):
        t = nums[i]
        if t in ('M', 'L'):
            pts.append((float(nums[i + 1]), float(nums[i + 2])))
            i += 3
        elif t == 'A':
            pts.append((float(nums[i + 6]), float(nums[i + 7])))
            i += 8
        else:
            i += 1
    return pts


def side_at(p, rect):
    x0, y0, x1, y1 = rect
    for nm, d in (('Left', abs(p[0] - x0)), ('Right', abs(p[0] - x1)), ('Top', abs(p[1] - y0)), ('Bottom', abs(p[1] - y1))):
        if d < 4.01:
            return nm
    return '?'


cases = []
for i in range(N):
    wa, wb, wc = random.choice(words), random.choice(words), random.choice(words)
    src = '{ direction: column }\n|box#a| "%s"\n|box#b| "%s"\n|box#c| "%s"\na -> c\n' % (wa, wb, wc)
    cases.append((wa, wb, wc, src))
with ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=16) as ex:
    res = list(ex.map(lambda c: run(c[3]), cases))
for (wa, wb, wc, src), (o, m, e) in zip(cases, res):
    ws = [float(w) for w in re.findall(r'<rect x="[^"]*" y="[^"]*" width="([^"]*)"', o)]
    d = re.search(r'<path d="(M[^"]*)"', o).group(1)
    pts = pts_of(d)
    ha, hb, hc = ws[0] / 2, ws[1] / 2, ws[2] / 2
    ra = (-ha, -120.5, ha, -65.5)
    rc = (-hc, 65.5, hc, 120.5)
    sa = side_at(pts[0], ra)
    sb = side_at(pts[-1], rc)
    cands = {}
    for l in e.splitlines():
        if l.startswith('CAND'):
            nm = l.split()[1]
            c = float(l.split('=')[1].split()[0])
            if nm not in cands:
                cands[nm] = c
    best = min(cands.values()) if cands else 0
    mine_choice = min(cands, key=lambda k: cands[k]) if cands else '-'
    ch = sa + '->' + sb
    print('a %6.2f b %6.2f c %6.2f  orig %-12s ours %-12s  d(orig-best)=%7.2f  %s' % (ha, hb, hc, ch, mine_choice, cands.get(ch, float('nan')) - best, 'OK' if o == m else ''))

#!/usr/bin/env python3
# Column a, b, c with `a -> c`: the original's chosen side pair vs our candidate costs.
import subprocess, re, os, tempfile, random, sys
from concurrent.futures import ThreadPoolExecutor
random.seed(int(sys.argv[1]) if len(sys.argv) > 1 else 1)
N = int(sys.argv[2]) if len(sys.argv) > 2 else 80
words = ['x', 'f', 'db', 'mm', 'WW', 'log', 'api', 'web', 'auth', 'user', 'cache', 'store', 'queue', 'Wor', 'Work', 'Worke', 'Worker', 'Gateway', 'Worker pool', 'iii', 'svc', 'Worker pool xx']


def run(src):
    d = tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix='/tmp/link2/cf.')
    open(d + '/r_in.lini', 'w').write(src)
    r = subprocess.run(['/workspace/executable', 'r_in.lini'], capture_output=True, cwd=d)
    env = dict(os.environ)
    env['LINI_DBG_ROUTE'] = '1'
    m = subprocess.run(['/tmp/bin-link2/executable', 'r_in.lini'], capture_output=True, cwd=d, env=env)
    os.remove(d + '/r_in.lini')
    os.rmdir(d)
    return r.stdout.decode(), m.stdout.decode(), m.stderr.decode()


def pts_of(d):
    nums = re.findall(r'[MLA]|-?[0-9.]+', d)
    pts = []
    i = 0
    while i < len(nums):
        t = nums[i]
        if t in ('M', 'L'):
            pts.append((float(nums[i + 1]), float(nums[i + 2])))
            i += 3
        elif t == 'A':
            pts.append((float(nums[i + 6]), float(nums[i + 7])))
            i += 8
        else:
            i += 1
    return pts


def side_at(p, rect):
    x0, y0, x1, y1 = rect
    for nm, d in (('Left', abs(p[0] - x0)), ('Right', abs(p[0] - x1)), ('Top', abs(p[1] - y0)), ('Bottom', abs(p[1] - y1))):
        if d < 4.01:
            return nm
    return '?'


cases = []
for i in range(N):
    wa, wb, wc = random.choice(words), random.choice(words), random.choice(words)
    src = '{ direction: column }\n|box#a| "%s"\n|box#b| "%s"\n|box#c| "%s"\na -> c\n' % (wa, wb, wc)
    cases.append((wa, wb, wc, src))
with ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=16) as ex:
    res = list(ex.map(lambda c: run(c[3]), cases))
for (wa, wb, wc, src), (o, m, e) in zip(cases, res):
    ws = [float(w) for w in re.findall(r'<rect x="[^"]*" y="[^"]*" width="([^"]*)"', o)]
    d = re.search(r'<path d="(M[^"]*)"', o).group(1)
    pts = pts_of(d)
    ha, hb, hc = ws[0] / 2, ws[1] / 2, ws[2] / 2
    ra = (-ha, -120.5, ha, -65.5)
    rc = (-hc, 65.5, hc, 120.5)
    sa = side_at(pts[0], ra)
    sb = side_at(pts[-1], rc)
    cands = {}
    for l in e.splitlines():
        if l.startswith('CAND'):
            nm = l.split()[1]
            c = float(l.split('=')[1].split()[0])
            if nm not in cands:
                cands[nm] = c
    best = min(cands.values()) if cands else 0
    mine_choice = min(cands, key=lambda k: cands[k]) if cands else '-'
    ch = sa + '->' + sb
    print('a %6.2f b %6.2f c %6.2f  orig %-12s ours %-12s  d(orig-best)=%7.2f  %s' % (ha, hb, hc, ch, mine_choice, cands.get(ch, float('nan')) - best, 'OK' if o == m else ''))

2	# For column a, b, c with `a -> c`: for each c label, scan b labels (sorted by width) and report the
3	# original's start side, to find the b width threshold where the choice flips.
4	import subprocess, re, os, tempfile, sys
5	from concurrent.futures import ThreadPoolExecutor
6	a = sys.argv[1]
7	cs = sys.argv[2].split(',')
8	rootx = sys.argv[3] if len(sys.argv) > 3 else ''
9	linkx = sys.argv[4] if len(sys.argv) > 4 else ''
10	bs = ['f', 'x', 'db', 'iii', 'mm', 'api', 'ap', 'apl', 'apr', 'apt', 'svc', 'log', 'web', 'auth', 'apim', 'user', 'store', 'cache', 'queue', 'Work', 'Worker', 'Gateway', 'Worker pool']
11	
12	
13	def run(src):
14	    d = tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix='/tmp/link2/th.')
15	    open(d + '/r_in.lini', 'w').write(src)
16	    r = subprocess.run(['/workspace/executable', 'r_in.lini'], capture_output=True, cwd=d)
17	    os.remove(d + '/r_in.lini')
18	    os.rmdir(d)
19	    return r.stdout.decode()
20	
21	
22	jobs = []
23	for c in cs:
24	    for b in bs:
25	        jobs.append((c, b, '{ direction: column; %s }\n|box#a| "%s"\n|box#b| "%s"\n|box#c| "%s"\na -> c %s\n' % (rootx, a, b, c, linkx)))
26	with ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=16) as ex:
27	    outs = list(ex.map(lambda j: run(j[2]), jobs))
28	rows = {}
29	for (c, b, _), o in zip(jobs, outs):
30	    ys = [float(v) for v in re.findall(r'translate\((-?[0-9.]+),? (-?[0-9.]+)\)', o) for v in [v[1]]]
31	    ws = [float(w) for w in re.findall(r'<rect x="[^"]*" y="[^"]*" width="([^"]*)"', o)]
32	    d = re.search(r'<path d="(M[^"]*)"', o).group(1)

# usage: thresh2.py WA WC w0 w1 step [rootx] [linkx]
import subprocess, re, os, tempfile, sys

wa, wc = float(sys.argv[1]), float(sys.argv[2])
w0, w1, st = float(sys.argv[3]), float(sys.argv[4]), float(sys.argv[5])

def run(src):

    r = subprocess.run(['/workspace/executable', 'r_in.lini'], capture_output=True, cwd=d)
    os.remove(d + '/r_in.lini')
    os.rmdir(d)
    return r.stdout.decode()


ws = []
w = w0
while w <= w1 + 1e-9:
    ws.append(round(w, 4))

jobs = ['{ direction: column; %s }\n|box#a| "a" { width: %s; }\n|box#b| "b" { width: %s; }\n|box#c| "c" { width: %s; }\na -> c %s\n' % (rootx, wa, w, wc, linkx) for w in ws]

        e = 'L' if xe < 0 else 'R'
    elif ye < YC:
        e = 'T'
    else:
        e = 'B'
    res.append('%g:%s' % (w, s + e))
print(' '.join(res))

#!/usr/bin/env python3
# Find the b-width threshold (BR -> LL/RR switch) by bisection for a parameterised column scene.
# usage: thresh3.py "template with {B}" lo hi
import subprocess, re, os, tempfile, sys
tmpl = sys.argv[1].replace('\\n', '\n')
lo, hi = float(sys.argv[2]), float(sys.argv[3])


def run(src):
    d = tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix='/tmp/link2/t3.')
    open(d + '/r_in.lini', 'w').write(src)
    r = subprocess.run(['/workspace/executable', 'r_in.lini'], capture_output=True, cwd=d)
    os.remove(d + '/r_in.lini')
    os.rmdir(d)
    return r.stdout.decode()


def side(w):
    o = run(tmpl.replace('{B}', '%.6f' % w))
    ys = [float(v[1]) for v in re.findall(r'translate\((-?[0-9.]+),(-?[0-9.]+)\)', o)]
    YA = ys[0]
    d = re.search(r'<path d="(M[^"]*)"', o).group(1)
    nums = [float(v) for v in re.findall(r'-?[0-9.]+', d)]
    x0, y0 = nums[0], nums[1]
    if abs(y0 - YA) < 0.01:
        return 'L' if x0 < 0 else 'R'
    return 'B' if y0 > YA else 'T'


slo, shi = side(lo), side(hi)
print('lo', lo, slo, 'hi', hi, shi)
if slo == shi:
    sys.exit(0)
for _ in range(30):
    mid = (lo + hi) / 2
    s = side(mid)
    if s == slo:
        lo = mid
    else:
        hi = mid
    if hi - lo < 1e-4:
        break
print('threshold %.4f (%s below, %s above)' % ((lo + hi) / 2, slo, shi))

# Column a, b, c (`a -> c`), a widest: scan a parameter and print the original's start side per value.
# usage: lrscan.py "template with {P}" v0 v1 step
import subprocess, re, os, tempfile, sys
from concurrent.futures import ThreadPoolExecutor
tmpl = sys.argv[1].replace('\\n', '\n')
v0, v1, st = float(sys.argv[2]), float(sys.argv[3]), float(sys.argv[4])
mine = os.environ.get('MINE')


def run(src, b='/workspace/executable'):
    d = tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix='/tmp/link2/lr.')
    open(d + '/r_in.lini', 'w').write(src)
    r = subprocess.run([b, 'r_in.lini'], capture_output=True, cwd=d)
    os.remove(d + '/r_in.lini')
    os.rmdir(d)
    return r.stdout.decode()


def side(o):
    tr = [(float(x), float(y)) for x, y in re.findall(r'translate\((-?[0-9.]+),(-?[0-9.]+)\)', o)]

#!/usr/bin/env python3
# Can floating-point rounding in a shifted frame explain LL vs RR choices?
import re, itertools
K = 16.0
obs = []
for l in open('/tmp/link2/lrg1.txt'):
    m = re.match(r'a=\s*(\d+) b=\s*(\d+) c=\s*(\d+)\s+(\S+)', l)
    a, b, c, cls = int(m.group(1)), int(m.group(2)), int(m.group(3)), m.group(4)
    if cls in ('LL', 'RR'):
        obs.append((a, b, c, cls))


def edges_lr(ws, frame):
    # returns the x lines of left and right sides in the given frame for widths ws (a, b, c)
    W = max(ws) + 2.0  # outer content width
    out = []
    for w in ws:
        ow = w + 2.0
        if frame == 'centre':
            x0 = -ow / 2
            x1 = ow / 2
        elif frame == 'left1':
            x0 = (W - ow) / 2
            x1 = x0 + ow
        elif frame == 'left2':
            cx = W / 2
            x0 = cx - ow / 2
            x1 = cx + ow / 2
        elif frame == 'left3':
            x0 = W / 2 - ow / 2
            x1 = W / 2 + ow / 2
        elif frame.startswith('pad'):
            p = float(frame[3:])
            cx = p + W / 2
            x0 = cx - ow / 2
            x1 = cx + ow / 2
        out.append((x0, x1))
    return out


def cost_side(ws, frame, side, prefix, order):
    e = edges_lr(ws, frame)
    a, b, c = e
    if side == 'L':
        base = a[0] - K
        lines = sorted({b[0] - K, c[0] - K})
        lines = [x for x in lines if base < x <= c[0] - K]
        pts = [base] + lines
    else:
        base = a[1] + K
        lines = sorted({b[1] + K, c[1] + K}, reverse=True)
        lines = [x for x in lines if c[1] + K <= x < base]
        pts = [base] + lines
    cost = prefix
    for p, q in zip(pts, pts[1:]):
        cost = cost + abs(q - p)
    if order == 'k_last':
        cost = cost + K
    return cost


frames = ['centre', 'left1', 'left2', 'left3'] + ['pad%d' % p for p in (8, 12, 16, 20, 24, 32, 40)]
for frame in frames:
    for prefix in (0.0, 300.0, 330.0, 16.0 + 32.0 + 186.0 + 32.0):
        for order in ('k_last', 'none'):
            ok = 0
            for a, b, c, cls in obs:
                ws = (a, b, c)
                if not (a >= b and a >= c):
                    # base hugs another box; skip (all RR)
                    ok += cls == 'RR'
                    continue
                cl = cost_side(ws, frame, 'L', prefix, order)
                cr = cost_side(ws, frame, 'R', prefix, order)
                pick = 'LL' if cl < cr else 'RR'
                ok += pick == cls
            print(frame, prefix, order, ok, '/', len(obs))

#!/usr/bin/env python3
# Row a, b, c with `a -> c`: original's start/end sides over a grid of heights.
import subprocess, re, os, tempfile, sys, itertools
from concurrent.futures import ThreadPoolExecutor
hs = [int(v) for v in sys.argv[1].split(',')]
link = sys.argv[2] if len(sys.argv) > 2 else 'a -> c'
extra = sys.argv[3] if len(sys.argv) > 3 else ''


def run(src, b='/workspace/executable'):
    d = tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix='/tmp/link2/ug.')
    open(d + '/r_in.lini', 'w').write(src)
    r = subprocess.run([b, 'r_in.lini'], capture_output=True, cwd=d)
    os.remove(d + '/r_in.lini')
    os.rmdir(d)
    return r.stdout.decode()


def sides(o, s_idx, e_idx):
    tr = [(float(x), float(y)) for x, y in re.findall(r'translate\((-?[0-9.]+),(-?[0-9.]+)\)', o)]
    ds = re.findall(r'<path d="(M[^"]*)"', o)
    if not ds:
        return '--'
    nums = [float(v) for v in re.findall(r'-?[0-9.]+', ds[0])]

    def side(px, py, c):
        if abs(px - c[0]) < 1e-6 and abs(py - c[1]) > 1e-6:
            return 'T' if py < c[1] else 'B'
        if abs(py - c[1]) < 1e-6:
            return 'L' if px < c[0] else 'R'
        return '?'
    return side(nums[0], nums[1], tr[s_idx]) + side(nums[-2], nums[-1], tr[e_idx])


s_idx, e_idx = (0, 2) if link.startswith('a') else (2, 0)
combos = list(itertools.product(hs, hs, hs))
srcs = ['{ %s }\n|box#a| "a" { height: %d; }\n|box#b| "b" { height: %d; }\n|box#c| "c" { height: %d; }\n%s\n' % (extra, a, b, c, link) for a, b, c in combos]
with ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=16) as ex:
    outs = list(ex.map(run, srcs))
    mine = list(ex.map(lambda s: run(s, '/tmp/bin-link2/executable'), srcs))
for (a, b, c), o, m in zip(combos, outs, mine):
    print('a=%3d b=%3d c=%3d  %s %s' % (a, b, c, sides(o, s_idx, e_idx), '' if o == m else 'DIFF(' + sides(m, s_idx, e_idx) + ')'))

#!/usr/bin/env python3
# For the 4-box column (auth / Worker pool / web / c), vary c's label inside a fixed-width box and
# report the natural width of the label's box and the original's L/R choice.
import subprocess, re, os, tempfile, sys
from concurrent.futures import ThreadPoolExecutor
labels = sys.argv[1].split(',')
W = sys.argv[2] if len(sys.argv) > 2 else '60'


def run(src):
    d = tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix='/tmp/link2/tx.')
    open(d + '/r_in.lini', 'w').write(src)
    r = subprocess.run(['/workspace/executable', 'r_in.lini'], capture_output=True, cwd=d)
    os.remove(d + '/r_in.lini')
    os.rmdir(d)
    return r.stdout.decode()


def nat(lbl):
    o = run('|box#c| "%s"\n' % lbl)
    return float(re.search(r'<rect x="[^"]*" y="[^"]*" width="([^"]*)"', o).group(1))


def side(lbl):
    o = run('{ direction: column }\n|box#a| "auth"\n|box#b| "Worker pool"\n|box#d| "web"\n|box#c| "%s" { width: %s; }\na -> c\n' % (lbl, W))
    d = re.search(r'<path d="M (-?[0-9.]+)', o).group(1)
    return 'L' if float(d) < 0 else 'R'


with ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=16) as ex:
    nats = list(ex.map(nat, labels))
    sides = list(ex.map(side, labels))
for l, n, s in sorted(zip(labels, nats, sides), key=lambda t: t[1]):
    print('%-10s nat %.3f  %s' % (l, n, s))

#!/usr/bin/env python3
# For the 4-box column (auth / Worker pool / web / c), vary c's label inside a fixed-width box and
# report the natural width of the label's box and the original's L/R choice.
import subprocess, re, os, tempfile, sys
from concurrent.futures import ThreadPoolExecutor
labels = sys.argv[1].split(',')
W = sys.argv[2] if len(sys.argv) > 2 else '60'


def run(src):
    d = tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix='/tmp/link2/tx.')
    open(d + '/r_in.lini', 'w').write(src)
    r = subprocess.run(['/workspace/executable', 'r_in.lini'], capture_output=True, cwd=d)
    os.remove(d + '/r_in.lini')
    os.rmdir(d)
    return r.stdout.decode()


def nat(lbl):
    o = run('|box#c| "%s"\n' % lbl)
    return float(re.search(r'<rect x="[^"]*" y="[^"]*" width="([^"]*)"', o).group(1))


def side(lbl):
    o = run('{ direction: column }\n|box#a| "auth"\n|box#b| "Worker pool"\n|box#d| "web"\n|box#c| "%s" { width: %s; }\na -> c\n' % (lbl, W))
    d = re.search(r'<path d="M (-?[0-9.]+)', o).group(1)
    return 'L' if float(d) < 0 else 'R'


with ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=16) as ex:
    nats = list(ex.map(nat, labels))
    sides = list(ex.map(side, labels))
for l, n, s in sorted(zip(labels, nats, sides), key=lambda t: t[1]):
    print('%-10s nat %.3f  %s' % (l, n, s))
